title: Ghana Cyber Security Authority official cites 4,938 reported cybercrimes in 2026 so far
date_note: Xinhua's dateline is Accra, 25 November; the page gives no earlier day.
summary: Xinhua reports that Jake France, head of Cybersecurity Technology Standards at Ghana's Cyber Security Authority, urged technology service providers to make cybersecurity a priority at the Tech in Ghana Accra 2026 conference. He said reported cybercrimes in Ghana increased to 4,938, compared to 4,604 cases in 2025 as a whole, with an associated financial loss of approximately 209 million Ghana cedis.
plain: A Ghanaian cybersecurity official says reported cybercrimes reached 4,938, against 4,604 in all of 2025, and urges technology firms to prioritise security.
exec: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority official says reported cybercrimes reached 4,938, compared to 4,604 in 2025 as a whole, with losses of approximately 209 million Ghana cedis.
action: The Cyber Security Authority official urges technology service providers to make cybersecurity a priority and to treat it as an investment.
geo_basis: Conference in Accra, Ghana, as stated by Xinhua
